title: Introduction to Statistics
prerequisites: Basic algebra and elementary functions; link the existing Mathematics books.

units.title: Statistical Reasoning, Populations and Evidence
scope: Population, sample, census, descriptive and inferential aims
Observational units, variables and parameters
Sampling variability versus bias
Summation notation and statistical reasoning
Misuse of statistics, association versus causation, ethical reporting
units.simulation: Optional finite-population sampling explorer; show selection bias without claiming inferential coverage.

units.title: Measurement, Data Collection and Data Quality
scope: Nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio scales
Qualitative, quantitative, discrete and continuous variables
Primary and secondary sources
Questionnaire construction, pilot studies and schedules
Missing values, recording errors, data dictionaries and reproducible cleaning

units.title: Classification, Frequency Tables and Cross-Tabulation
scope: Individual and grouped data
Nominal limits and actual class boundaries
Equal and unequal intervals; frequency density
Relative and cumulative frequencies
One-way and two-way tables; conditional percentages and Simpson's paradox
units.simulation: Interactive histogram with variable bin width; enforce area proportional to frequency.

units.title: Statistical Graphics and Exploratory Data Analysis
scope: Bar charts, pie charts, histograms and cumulative plots
Stem-and-leaf displays, dot plots and scatter diagrams
Five-number summaries, quartile conventions and box plots
Outlier flags versus deletion decisions
Axis choices, misleading graphics and visual comparison
units.simulation: Box-plot and raw-data explorer with visible quartile convention and outlier flags.

units.title: Location, Quantiles and Weighted Summaries
scope: Arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means
Median, mode, percentiles and percentile rank
Weighted means and combined groups
Grouped-data approximations and their limits
Transformation properties and sensitivity to extreme observations
units.simulation: Move-an-outlier experiment comparing mean and median.

units.title: Variation, Standardization and Relative Dispersion
scope: Range, interquartile range and absolute deviations
Population and sample variance conventions
Standard deviation, pooled summaries and decomposition
Coefficient of variation and valid scale assumptions
Standard scores, descriptive empirical patterns and Chebyshev bounds
problem_types: Assess use of coefficient of variation
units.simulation: Variance decomposition explorer with direct independently computed sums.

units.title: Moments, Skewness, Kurtosis and Distribution Shape
scope: Raw and central moments; relationships and translation
Empirical moments and standardized moments
Skewness measures and interpretation
Kurtosis versus excess kurtosis; estimator conventions
Tail behavior, outliers and misleading shape summaries
problem_types: Derive central moments from raw moments
units.simulation: Distribution-shape explorer using synthetic data with documented generation parameters.

units.title: Correlation and Measures of Association
scope: Bivariate tables, covariance and Pearson correlation
Ranks, ties, Spearman correlation and Kendall tau
Kendall concordance among multiple rankings
Point-biserial, biserial, fourfold/phi and tetrachoric correlations with assumptions
Correlation ratio, intraclass correlation, nonlinear association and interpretation limits
problem_types: Choose a coefficient for variable types
Identify nonlinear dependence missed by Pearson correlation
units.simulation: Scatterplot explorer with movable points and a warning that correlation is not causal.

units.title: Simple Regression and an Integrated Statistical Investigation
scope: Descriptive simple linear regression and the least-squares criterion
Derivation of normal equations, slope and intercept
Fitted values, residuals and sums-of-squares decomposition
Interpretation, extrapolation and diagnostic limitations
Reproducible Python/R descriptive analysis and a complete data-to-report case study
problem_types: Analyze and report an original synthetic dataset
units.simulation: Least-squares line explorer; compare hand-calculated and plotted residual sums.

coverage_review: Outline covers the selected introductory syllabus, including less common association coefficients. Check every item against the detailed course section before claiming complete coverage. Inference and advanced regression remain in later books.
next_action: Draft Unit 1 with original prose and independently checked problems; save checkpoints before writing later units. No textbook has yet been completed or published.
